tasks.title: Compose setups receive a validated persistent console encryption key through secrets-init
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Behavior: Host key, secrets-init files mode, secrets-init generate mode and Compose; corresponding Checks for init-secrets, check-setup rule 7, secrets-init and Compose config. Implement one coherent provisioning path: make_token creates console-secret-key without overwriting; strict host key validation and comparison with every probe token and the admin token occurs before any files-mode write when /out/console exists; generate mode keeps a valid key and refuses an invalid existing key without replacing it. Preserve path/permission checks, atomic writes and no-secret output. Set PULSE_CONSOLE_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/run/pulse/secret-key in full/dev/demo using existing volumes, ports and dependencies. Update existing secrets-init console fixtures with valid distinct key inputs. Rollout order step 1: deploy merges before console, and the #562 console ignores the key setting and file; no console change is needed for this task. Keep the CLI unit suite green; T2 connects CLI-generated installs to the new shared helper, and T3 preserves the legacy e2e flow.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; host console-secret-key is a regular mode-600 file with 64 lowercase hex characters and one LF, safely created without secret output; a second run preserves its SHA-256. Rule 7 covers key mode/content/preservation and a missing-key case fails with rule 7. Existing token, symlink and static-setup cases still pass.

exit 0; with /out/console, files mode writes /out/console/secret-key byte-equal to the host key without its one LF, owned 1000:1000 mode 400. Missing, malformed and token-equal keys respectively give /in/console-secret-key: is missing; run scripts/init-secrets.sh, /in/console-secret-key: must hold 64 lowercase hex characters, and /in/console-secret-key: must differ from every token, before writing any output file. Include equality with a probe token and with the admin token. Symlink/nonregular/group-or-other access is refused. Without /out/console no key is read. Generate mode creates 64 lowercase hex, preserves its SHA-256 on rerun, and an invalid existing key gives /out/console/secret-key: must hold 64 lowercase hex characters with the old bytes unchanged.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; full/dev/demo console environment names /run/pulse/secret-key using the existing console secrets volume; minimal, ports, depends_on and image pins are unchanged

tasks.title: CLI installs generate a console key and refuse to replace an invalid existing key
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Behavior: CLI; all CLI Checks, including isSecretKeyContent, generation only when console is enabled, random draw after tokens/before installId, KNOWN_FILES, preflight with no writes on an invalid key, --force byte preservation and rendered console env. Adapt deterministic comparison fixtures to the specified draw order. Keep valid-file, symlink, permission, lock and atomic-write protections; a valid existing key is preserved rather than treated as an ordinary replaceable token. No-console/minimal rendering remains unchanged. This completes CLI use of the secrets-init helper from T1 and must work with the unchanged pinned console images.

acceptance.command: bun test --coverage cli/tokens.test.ts cli/init.test.ts cli/write-install.test.ts cli/render-compose.test.ts
acceptance.expected: 0 fail in selected tests; focused coverage may exit nonzero. Console-enabled init writes secrets/console-secret-key matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}\n$ in mode 600 after drawing tokens and before installId; no-console init writes no key. --force preserves a valid key byte-for-byte and refuses an invalid key with secrets/console-secret-key: is not a valid key (64 lowercase hex characters); fix or remove it before any write. Strict content accepts no LF or one LF only; malformed cases from the spec fail. Rendered console env points to /run/pulse/secret-key; minimal without console remains byte-equal to the existing fixture.

exit 0; CLI lint, typecheck and the full tests meet 80% line coverage. Generation/writer/render integration and deterministic fixtures remain green without changing packages, pins, configuration conventions or secret-write protections.

tasks.title: Deploy keeps the #562 setup e2e green and prepares the two-factor flow for the console PR
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Behavior: e2e/totp.mjs and all e2e/console-setup.sh flow selection and steps; Acceptance evidence 12 and preparation for 13; all final Checks, Completion evidence, Rollout order step 1 and applicable Security impact checklist. Preserve shared steps 1-5 and the #562 legacy steps 7-10; step 6 detects legacy from /sign-in?setup=done or two-factor from /account/authenticator. E2E_CONSOLE_FLOW defaults to auto for unset/empty, can force legacy or two-factor, and invalid values exit 2 before any request or Compose call; unknown Location and forced-flow mismatch use the literal spec errors. Keep the complete two-factor algorithm together (steps 7-13): separate cookie jars, enrolment, ten codes, fresh-step TOTP, recovery replay, sign out all, persisted-key recreation and file/sidecar scans with owner-email positive control. Use Origin and page CSRF, bounded waits and the independent RFC helper self-check; never print secrets. Run deploy main's existing legacy console on a fresh dev volume, the touched CI job commands and pinned-image full/demo/CLI checks. The two-factor flow's first real execution is acceptance 13 in the console PR's deploy-dev job after this child merges; it is not a prerequisite of this deploy PR. Document strict key format, upgrade by rerunning init-secrets for existing full/dev installs, database+key backup, lost-key/recovery path, E2E_CONSOLE_FLOW and both flows, and full/demo/CLI 2FA activation only with a later console pin bump. No interim dev failure is allowed; do not bump images or edit workflows outside Files.

acceptance.expected: exit 0; helper checks the RFC 6238 Appendix B six-digit value 287082 for ASCII seed 12345678901234567890 at T=59 before printing one line matching ^[0-9]+ [0-9]{6}$. Production algorithm is SHA-1, 30-second step, six digits. The helper prints no key. The base32 test input comes from RFC 4648 section 6 as recorded in Acceptance evidence 4.
exit 2; stderr is usage: e2e/totp.mjs <base32 key>; no key or code is printed.
exit 2; stderr is usage: e2e/totp.mjs <base32 key>; only A-Z and 2-7 are accepted, without padding.
exit 2; stderr is E2E_CONSOLE_FLOW must be auto, legacy or two-factor, before any request or docker compose call; run with no stack.

Auto detection prints ok: 6 POST /setup/owner complete 303 flow legacy; legacy steps 7-10 stay unchanged and pass with the key provisioned and ignored. Unset/empty E2E_CONSOLE_FLOW select auto; on separate fresh-volume runs forced legacy succeeds and forced two-factor fails at step 6 with step 6: console has the legacy flow, E2E_CONSOLE_FLOW=two-factor. Review the two-factor branch against the literal steps 7-13 in this spec; its first real run is console CI deploy-dev (acceptance 13), after this deploy change merges. Record actual legacy ok lines in the PR, with no secrets.

Review flow selection, shared steps 1-5, unchanged legacy steps 7-10 and two-factor steps 7-13 against spec literals; do not claim two-factor runtime evidence before the console PR.
